summary: The Elders of Ancha: a long island of fishing villages ruled by a moot, with a reef whose drowned voices the fishers will not cross at night.

elders_moot.name: The Elders' Moot
elders_moot.desc: The elders of every village sit in a ring on the beach, the eldest on a driftwood log. A matter is settled when the ring has been round three times.

eldest_speaks.name: The Eldest Speaks
eldest_speaks.desc: Nara's eldest wears the island's name and speaks for the moot with a voice that carries from point to point. Her words are repeated at every hearth before the tide turns.

night_custom.name: No Boat at Night
night_custom.desc: After dark the boats are drawn up above the tide-line and the lamps are shaded. The catch is smaller and the fishers come home.

reef_lights.name: Lights on the Reef
reef_lights.desc: Beacon-fires burn on the reef at dusk and are fed with driftwood until dawn. Passing ships steer by them and are grateful.

ancha_fisheries.name: Fisheries of Ancha
ancha_fisheries.desc: Smoke-houses stand in every village, and the smell of drying fish carries across the water. Nara's smoked fish is sold on every quay from the isles to the coast.

the_reef_at_night.title: The Reef at Night
the_reef_at_night.desc: Young fishers want to cross the reef at night, where the catch is best. The old ones say that voices are heard on the water there, and that no boat has ever come back who answered.

the_silent_reef.title: The Silent Reef
the_silent_reef.desc: Since the storm year, nobody has heard the voices on the reef. The fishers say that a stranger carried the stranded children home through the surf, and that afterwards the sea went quiet.

focuses.name: The Elders of Ancha
focuses.desc: Nara is the island of Ancha, a long coast of fishing villages ruled by a moot of elders. Its eldest speaks for all, and wants nothing from the wider world but fair prices for smoked fish.

focuses.name: The Elders' Moot
focuses.desc: The elders meet on the beach at the new moon, and the villages send word of their needs. The moot has never voted: it has waited, and the matter has settled itself.

focuses.name: Voices of the Villages
focuses.desc: Each village sends a speaker to the moot, chosen by the women who mend the nets and the men who mind the boats. The speakers stand, one at a time, and are heard.

focuses.name: The Elders' Law
focuses.desc: The old law is cut on a row of driftwood posts at the head of the beach, and the posts are replaced as they rot. A fisher who breaks it must repair a post.

focuses.name: The Eldest Speaks
focuses.desc: The eldest takes the island's own name and a staff of grey wood, and speaks first in every gathering. Nobody on Ancha can remember a time when she did not.

focuses.name: The Reef of Voices
focuses.desc: Off the eastern point lies a reef where drowned voices are said to call ships onto the rocks. The fishers will not cross it at night, and nobody asks them why.

focuses.name: No Boat at Night
focuses.desc: The custom is made law: after dark the boats stay on the sand. The catch is smaller, the funerals are fewer, and the elders say the trade is fair.

focuses.name: Lights on the Reef
focuses.desc: A line of lamps is lit on the rocks each dusk, and a keeper is sent out in a skiff to trim them. The reef is still dangerous, but it is no longer dark.

focuses.name: The Reef Guides
focuses.desc: Fishers who know the reef by heart are paid to guide passing ships through the channel by daylight. They carry a bell, a pole and a very long memory.

focuses.name: The Silent Reef
focuses.desc: Since the storm year the voices have gone quiet, and the fishers have begun to talk of crossing the reef by night again. The elders listen and say little.

focuses.name: Fisherfolk of Ancha
focuses.desc: Ancha has more fishers than farmers, and more boats than roads. A new fish-quay is built at each of the larger villages, and the nets are mended in the open air.

focuses.name: Smoked Fish for the Ships
focuses.desc: Smoked fish keeps for a year, and ships' captains buy it by the barrel. The smokers sell from the quay and keep their recipes in their families.

focuses.name: The Net-Menders
focuses.desc: Net-menders work in long sheds on the beaches, twisting hemp into line and knotting line into mesh. A new net is blessed with the first catch.

focuses.name: The Catch of Ancha
focuses.desc: Salted, smoked and dried fish fill the storehouses of every village, and the elders see to it that no household goes without. A lean winter on Ancha is a quiet one.
